findings.evidence: Comparison.lean:50-51: `theorem forall_map_I_mul_eq_iff {L : ℂ →L[ℝ] V} {A : V →L[ℝ] V} (hA : ∀ v, A (A v) = -v) : (∀ w, L (I * w) = A (L w)) ↔ L 1 + A (L I) = 0`. Its proof uses only `map_add`, `map_smul` and `module`.
findings.fix: Move it to an early linear-algebra or complex-structure file, for example next to the complex-module material in `TauCeti/Geometry/Symplectic/Complex/Module/Basic.lean` or a `ContinuousLinearMap` file on ℂ. Keep it public there and import it here.
findings.issue: `forall_map_I_mul_eq_iff` only involves Mathlib types (`ℂ →L[ℝ] V`, an endomorphism with `A ∘ A = -id`) and does not depend on the weak equation. It is general infrastructure, but it lives in a leaf file that imports the manifold, Floer and JHolomorphic modules, so linear-algebra consumers cannot reach it cheaply.

findings.evidence: The grep of `namespace IsWeakCauchyRiemannHalfOn` (lines 161-199) finds only `continuousOn`, `memWkpLoc_one`, `ae_eq_of_hasWeakFDerivOn`, `mono`, `mono_exponent` and `isWeakCauchyRiemannOn_interior`.
findings.fix: Add `IsWeakCauchyRiemannHalfOn.memLpLoc : MemLpLoc p U u` and `IsWeakCauchyRiemannHalfOn.completeSpace`. Also add the half-plane derivative-independence characterization in terms of `MemWkpLoc p U 1 u`.
findings.issue: The file builds both predicates in parallel, but `IsWeakCauchyRiemannHalfOn` has no `memLpLoc` or `completeSpace` accessor and no `isWeakCauchyRiemannHalfOn_iff_forall_hasWeakFDerivOn`. `IsWeakCauchyRiemannOn` has all three (lines 106, 114, 151).

findings.evidence: Line 202: `theorem isWeakCauchyRiemannHalfOn_coe_iff : IsWeakCauchyRiemannHalfOn p (Ω : Set ℂ) J η u ↔ IsWeakCauchyRiemannOn p Ω J η u` has no attribute. Its right-hand side is strictly simpler and does not loop.
findings.issue: `isWeakCauchyRiemannHalfOn_coe_iff` rewrites the half-plane predicate on an open set to the canonical open-set predicate, and `isWeakCauchyRiemannOn_const_iff` (line 244) gives the characteristic form for constant maps. Both are normal-form rewrites, and neither is tagged `@[simp]`.

findings.evidence: Line 341: `fderiv ℝ id z I + (I • ContinuousLinearMap.id ℝ ℂ) (fderiv ℝ id z 1) ≠ 0`. The roadmap (PSHCA README:870-871) asks only that the swapped definition reverse the verdicts, not for exported `fderiv` lemmas.
findings.fix: State the roadmap check at the predicate level, for example by defining the swapped variant locally and proving the reversed verdicts. Otherwise turn these into `example`s or `private` lemmas, or give them names scoped to the check, such as `IsWeakCauchyRiemannOn.swapped_id_ne_zero`.
findings.issue: `fderiv_id_swapped` and `fderiv_conj_swapped` (line 346) are public root-namespace `TauCeti.fderiv_*` lemmas. They state one-off numeric facts about `I • id`, not reusable facts about `fderiv`, and they do not mention the predicate. The names read as general derivative API.

summary: The predicates and core API are sound, but a general linear-algebra lemma sits in a heavy comparison file, the half-plane predicate lacks accessors the open-set predicate has, normal-form lemmas lack `@[simp]`, and two roadmap checks are published as root-namespace `fderiv_*` lemmas with misleading names.
